title: Week 9 Fantasy Football standouts: Week 10 early waiver wire adds - CBS Sports
description: Darren Waller is carving out a heavy target share in Carolina, while Tank Dell's big-play ability and Shedeur San
body:
Darren Waller is carving out a heavy target share in Carolina, while Tank Dell's big-play ability and Shedeur Sanders' Superflex upside make them priority targets before Tuesday night
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:56 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We saw three more quarterback debuts in Week 9 of the NFL season which should give you a snapshot of where we're at in the Fantasy football season. I joked with Adam Aizer that this is the season from hell in Fantasy but the reality is that it's the season of creativity. We've all had to be extra creative with our rosters, start/sit decisions and streaming plays at positions that normally feel locked in. The result has been a slew of standout players on a weekly basis that at times appear like they come out of nowhere. That has led us to more waiver wire options in any given week. Let's take a look at several standouts from Week 9 that should be on your waiver wire radar for Week 10.Early waiver wire adds for Week 10 Darren Waller, TE, Panthers The Panthers continue to look for different ways to use the short passing game as an extension of their run game in large part due to their issues protecting Bryce Young against four-man pass rushes. Waller allows Young to isolate a mismatch presnap because defensive attention is focused on McMillan, Coker and Hubbard. This led to an excellent connection in Week 9, as Young and Waller hooked up for 90 yards and a touchdown on 8 targets. Waller was one of nine players to see double-digit targets in Week 9. For that alone, he should be on your early waiver wire radar. Tank Dell, WR, TexansHe's back, baby! We saw a glimpse of what Dell is capable of in the Texans' Week 9 win as he ripped off a long touchdown reception. He found another big play later by getting behind the Chargers secondary and has emerged as one of the deep threats in this offense. Dell is still working his way back and trying to find his footing and role in the new Texans scheme, but his big-play upside and history as an every-week Fantasy starter before the injury should be enough to stash him on your bench for now.Shedeur Sanders, QB, BrownsCredit where it's due -- Sanders looked so much more comfortable in Todd Monken's scheme than he ever did with Kevin Stefanski. To be fair, most quarterbacks do. Sanders spread the ball around, and it resulted in a career day for rookie first-round pick K.C. Concepcion. Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol but if he misses another game then Sanders is a must-roster player in Superflex formats. 
Justice Hill, RB, Ravens The Ravens were looking for unique ways to generate offense in Week 9 and that included using the wildcat. Hill racked up 85 rushing yards, a touchdown and three more receptions. A report surfaced later in the week that the Giants were poking around about trading for Hill. With both Cam Skattebo and Tryone Tracy Jr. injured, and Devin Singletary struggling in his first start, Hill could be a sneaky add. Standout Fantasy performancesKayshon Boutte, WR, TexansWith C.J. Stroud seeing the field post-snap at an elite level and throwing the football even more accurately, every Texans playmaker is worth considering as a bench stash. Boutte broke out with 125 yards and two touchdowns in Week 10. Keep an eye on the former Patriots big-play threat. 
Tee Higgins, WR, BengalsHiggins has maintained WR1 upside every week without the touchdowns, but we knew they were coming. They did in Week 9. Higgins caught two touchdowns in Week 9, and you'd be hard-pressed to find many receivers you'd rather start on a weekly basis.

title: Army vs. Navy 2026 uniforms: Black Knights unveil tribute to 'Ivy Soldiers' for annual rivalry game - CBS Sports
description: Army will honor the division's legacy with intricately detailed threads as they look to
body:
Army will honor the division's legacy with intricately detailed threads as they look to snap a two-game skid against Navy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Army Football
            
            

    
        Army will sport an "organic camouflage" look for its Dec. 12 rivalry showdown with Navy, as the Black Knights don special uniforms that will pay tribute to the 4th Infantry Division. Known as the "Ivy Soldiers," the division boasts a legacy dating back to World War I.The threads will specifically pay homage to 4th Infantry Division soldiers from the 2014-19 Operation Atlantic Resolve. As the Black Knights seek to snap a two-game losing streak against the Midshipmen, they'll do so in threads loaded with symbolism. "In the 25 years since the attacks on September 11th, Ivy Soldiers have been at the forefront in answering the nation's call," said narrator Michael Strahan on Army's announcement of the uniforms. "We will strive to emulate their dominance of any type of battlefield and consistent capability to always be ready and forward when we take the field against our rivals."Details go all the way down to the cleats, which incorporate 3D-embossed ivy vines weaving into the edges of Nike's swoosh. Above the numbers on the jersey backs — where player names would be emblazoned for most teams — each of Army's uniforms will simply read "Ivy soldier."
A total of 25 Ivy Soldiers have earned the Medal of Honor during the Division's 100+ year history. The early line in this year's game, which will be played at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, favors Navy by 2.5.

title: Gotham FC, Seattle Reign slam 'atrocious' pitch conditions after NWSL playoff clash - CBS Sports
description: Gotham benefitted from a fourth-minute own goal in Sunday's quarterfinal, which was the only goal of a game that
body:
Gotham benefitted from a fourth-minute own goal in Sunday's quarterfinal, which was the only goal of a game that made more noise because of the field
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:02 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        HARRISON, N.J. – Gotham FC head coach Juan Carlos Amoros criticized the field conditions at Sports Illustrated Stadium during the team's 1-0 win over the Seattle Reign on Sunday, a complaint that highlighted the infrastructure battles the league is grappling with during this season's playoffs.The NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 in the build-up to Sunday's quarterfinal over the quality of the pitch, which appears to have been overworked in recent weeks. Gotham are a secondary tenant at the stadium, which is owned by New Jersey's Hudson County and is primarily the home of the Red Bull New York. The MLS team played their regular season finale on Saturday evening, less than 24 hours before the 12:30 p.m. local time kickoff for the NWSL match. The stadium also hosted a rugby doubleheader the previous week, the scars of which were easy to spot over the course of Sunday's game."I feel the obligation to almost apologize for the state of the pitch," Amoros said post-match. "I think at this level, in this kind of game, as a league, we should be having a better surface. Unfortunately, our football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn't but luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt and the game was what it was."Players on both teams complained of the playing conditions, including Gotham's Jaelin Howell, who worked her way back from an ankle issue in time for Sunday's match.
"Obviously it's pretty sandy out there and so a little unstable but I want to be able to give my all to the team and everything I got and so obviously can't think about that," Howell said. "The other team has to play on that, too, so we acknowledged it and we moved on and I think that our team managed it pretty well for the most part."The Reign's Jess Fishlock, a member of Seattle's squad since the inaugural NWSL season in 2013 who played the final match of her career, was more harsh in her assessment of the field."We performed so well for this group of players to come against a team like that at home on this field, which is atrocious, just saying it out loud," she said.
Her comments were echoed by Reign coach Laura Harvey, who has worked in and around the league since its inception."Let's be real, there's no way a playoff game should be played on that shit," she told ESPN post-match. "I just can't believe they've allowed it. They knew it last week."Amoros said the field conditions ultimately impacted Gotham's ability to perform on Sunday, the NWSL Shield winners stringing together a performance he described as "not the best football match that you will ever see."
"When you play on a pitch like that, you cannot be thinking of the next action or what you're gonna do once you get that ball," he said. "You need to be looking at the ball because he can bounce at any given time. Plus, it just changes the whole dynamic of the game and it changes the dynamic of how we play. We adapted certain things. We adapted certain things on the game plan. We had to be a bit more direct and certain situations but it definitely affected the way we played, yes."Gotham will conclude play at Sports Illustrated Stadium next Sunday at 3 p.m. local time in the NWSL semifinals against the Kansas City Current. The Red Bulls, who missed the MLS Cup playoffs for a second consecutive season, will host another match the night before, this time a friendly against Club America during the men's international break.Gotham's vulnerabilities on displayThe pitch was an understandable obstacle for both teams but Gotham's struggles did not end there. The reigning champions, who are favored to win the championship for the third time in four seasons after winning the Shield, were second-best against the lowest-seeded team in the postseason. They benefitted from a fourth minute own goal from Jordyn Bugg, forced by standout Jaedyn Shaw, but were unable to actually assert any sort of dominance as the game progressed.
Gotham did not take a single shot on target over the course of the game, their six shots totaling just 0.17 expected goals. The Reign were not all that much better but momentum shifted their way in the second half, eventually racking up 11 shots and 0.54 expected goals. The visitors were stymied by Gotham defenders Tierna Davidson and Jess Carter, as well as 2024 goalkeeper of the year Ann-Katrin Berger."She literally does it on a consistent basis," Shaw said about Berger. "It's crazy the kind of saves that she makes and I feel like she makes a worldly save at least once a game and I mean I think it's hard enough getting through a back line but to get through Ann is a whole other task and I think we're all really grateful to have her back there. I know I am as an attacker and I think we all just have full trust in her ability and she's just such an integral part of our team and the way that we like to play as well. Even from the goal, she's such a big piece of the way that we play and our style."
Gotham's attack, though, had no such excuses. Midfielder Rose Lavelle exited the match at halftime as the coaching staff manages her minutes after dealing with a knock in recent weeks, her exit diluting their attack. Forward Sam Kerr, meanwhile, failed to register a single shot and took just 23 touches over the course of 90 minutes in an absent performance during an inconsistent return to the NWSL. The Australia international has scored just four goals in 18 games since joining Gotham in July, despite the fact that she has racked up 9.67 expected goals along the way.
Amoros credited the Reign for their ability to lock out Gotham's defense."I think they did a good job trying to stop certain situations," he said. "I think that was the key. They did really well on the press. They were first and second in a lot of the duels and they obviously play short passes to then go diagonal, which obviously then is something difficult to defend and something that is a lot more doable than probably over a style of play. It's just different and we had issues with those situations to defend. At the same time, we defended them. I think that's the key."Shaw, who attempted to spearhead a lifeless Gotham attack, described a disjointed performance that the team will hope not to replicate the following week."I think we just need to be cleaner on the ball," Shaw said. "Obviously, the surface doesn't really help but  just in general, I think we can be more comfortable on the ball, facing forward and just be clinical in our passes, which I think will help us get to the final third a little bit more with more quality chances on goal."

schema.headline: Gotham FC, Seattle Reign slam 'atrocious' pitch conditions after NWSL playoff clash - CBS Sports

title: Patrick Mahomes injury update: MRI reveals no significant damage to Chiefs QB's elbow - CBS Sports
description: An MRI revealed no significant injury after Mahomes' right elbow bent awkwardly
body:
An MRI revealed no significant injury after Mahomes' right elbow bent awkwardly
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:35 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Late in the first half of their blowout victory over the New York Jets, the Kansas City Chiefs got a significant scare. Patrick Mahomes dropped back to pass on a second-and-4 play coming out of the two-minute warning, and as he attempted to throw the ball downfield, his arm was hit by Jets edge rusher David Bailey. His elbow bent awkwardly backward, and he left the field with his right arm hanging by his side.Mahomes already underwent an MRI after the game and it did not reveal a significant injury, according to ESPN. He will be monitored for pain and swelling throughout the week.  
Mahomes ultimately didn't have to miss a snap because the Jets recovered the fumble on the play, and by the time the Chiefs got the ball back, Mahomes had gotten his arm warm while throwing on the sideline. He returned to play the rest of the game and finished the day 23 of 31 for 242 yards and two touchdowns, each on passes to Kenneth Walker III.Mahomes, later in his postgame interview, said he didn't feel like himself at first when he came back into the game after the scare, but that things gradually improved as he settled into the second half.
"I felt like out of the half, I wasn't throwing the ball the way I wanted to," he said. "As the game went on — and we continued to work through it and it kind of got warmed back up — I thought I started throwing the ball better towards the end of the second half. That will be important this week is kind of getting the swelling and the fluid out of it so I can be ready to go from the first snap next week."Mahomes further noted that he felt just fine after the game, but that he would have to go through the usual process to get himself ready for the Chiefs' Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons.
"I feel good now," he said. "Obviously, you get the win and the adrenaline's pumping. I'm sure I'll be sore tomorrow, but we'll get right to it. We'll get to work on it, and we'll get ourselves ready to go. It's great to get the win now, now it's about getting ourselves ready for next week."

schema.headline: Patrick Mahomes injury update: MRI reveals no significant damage to Chiefs QB's elbow - CBS Sports

title: Puka Nacua injury: Rams WR to undergo MRI after suffering knee injury on final snap, per report - CBS Sports
description: The Rams do not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but the wide receiver will undergo i
body:
The Rams do not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but the wide receiver will undergo imaging on Monday to confirm
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images
            
            

    
        The Los Angeles Rams are holding their breath over the status of star wideout Puka Nacua. The All-Pro pass catcher is set to undergo an MRI on his knee after injuring it late in the team's Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders, according to a report from ESPN. The team reportedly does not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging set to be done on Monday will determine the severity of the injury. Nacua suffered the injury on the final offensive snap of the game for Los Angeles with 1:44 remaining in the fourth quarter. He took a third-and-11 handoff from Matthew Stafford for a 5-yard gain. Nacua got up after a hard hit, but the injury will now be further evaluated. 
This injury dampens what was otherwise a stellar day for the wideout. He finished with 14 receptions on 19 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown, while adding 20 yards rushing. Nacua was the key to the Rams' success in the 20-13 victory that helped bring Los Angeles back over .500 on the season. 
Nacua is slated to miss time, which further dents what is already a banged-up receiver room. The Rams have already placed fellow wideout Davante Adams on injured reserve due to a ruptured hamstring he suffered in Week 6 against the Cardinals. That injury is expected to sideline him for anywhere from six to 10 weeks when he suffered it. This isn't the first injury Nacua has sustained this season, previously missing time this season with a hip injury. When he's been on the field, however, he's been among the best wideouts in the NFL and has caught a touchdown in four of his last five games played. 
If he's going to miss any time with this latest injury, it could embolden the Rams to make a move for a receiver prior to Tuesday's trade deadline.

title: Drew Lock suffers oblique injury, Week 10 status up in the air: Seahawks could have to start Jalen Milroe - CBS Sports
description: Lock was already filling in for Sam Darnold, who missed Week 9 with quad and rib injuries
body:
Lock was already filling in for Sam Darnold, who missed Week 9 with quad and rib injuries
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Drew Lock sustained an oblique injury in the Seattle Seahawks' Week 9 win over the Arizona Cardinals, and his status for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders is uncertain, Mike Macdonald said. The injury briefly sent Lock to the medical tent.Lock entered the game dealing with elbow tendinitis and was only playing because Sam Darnold was out due to quad and ribs injuries. Darnold suffered the quad injury neat the end of Seattle's Week 8 loss to the Chicago Bears and has been playing through a cracked rib.Lock, making his second start in place of Darnold this season, went 19 for 28 for 175 yards and a touchdown in the 17-3 victory., though he was clearly not 100%.
If neither Lock nor Darnold can play in Week 10, the Seahawks (5-4) would turn to third-string quarterback Jalen Milroe. They also have Adrian Martinez on their practice squad.
The Seahawks have little room for error. Entering "Sunday Night Football," the reigning champs were the No. 8 seed in the NFC, one spot out of the playoffs.Who is Jalen Milroe?The Seahawks took Milroe, an Alabama product, in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft.Milroe, now 23, had an up-and-down career with the Crimson Tide. In 2023 as a redshirt sophomore, he threw for 2,834 yards, 23 touchdowns and just six interceptions and added 531 yards and 12 touchdowns on the ground. He finished sixth in Heisman Trophy voting. That seemed to set the stage for a monster 2024, but instead, Milroe regressed as a passer and threw 11 interceptions. He still had 726 yards and 20 touchdowns on the ground, but it was not the follow-up he had been hoping for.
Should he be needed next week, Milroe would drastically alter the Seahawks' attack, making it likely more run-heavy. He has played three career NFL snaps and ran on all three for a total of 4 yards. Seattle did have one of its better ground performances Sunday with 120 yards, and the Raiders do struggle to defend the run.

title: Fantasy football Week 9 stock watch: Buy low, sell high and win your trades - CBS Sports
description: Frustrated managers are ready to sell after back-to-back near-misses at the goal line, opening the door to land a
body:
Frustrated managers are ready to sell after back-to-back near-misses at the goal line, opening the door to land a top-20 PPR running back at a steep discount
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:29 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There's no better time than now to strike while the iron is hot in your Fantasy football leagues on the trade market. Improving your roster by buying low or selling high on players due for regression (both positive and negative) is an excellent way to maximize your chances of winning your league. Let's take a look at several standout players from the Week 9 action and what to do moving forward with each one.Cincinnati 34 – Atlanta 17BUY LOW, BUT ONLY IF YOU'RE 6-3 OR BETTER: Drake LondonLondon saw a lot of Cincinnati's top cornerback D.J. Turner, and London also drew two pass interference penalties in the end zone. That's my way of excusing this subpar performance. I still think he'll be a good WR2 going forward with WR1 upside. But if you wan to trade for London, be aware that he gets the Chiefs, a bye and the Vikings in his next three weeks. The schedule gets much better after that. BUY VERY LOW: Chase BrownLast week, Brown had a TD catch called back. This week, he got stopped inside the 1-yard line. He still has only one touchdown this season! And now, people are sick of him. Brown managers will be more willing than ever to sell him, and you can take advantage. What are you getting in Brown? A Top 20 RB who (in PPR) should still be better than Blake Corum, Ollie Gordon, and the Jets RBs.New Orleans 23 - Cleveland 22KEEP IN MIND: Overtime was huge for these two quarterbacks. Both scored more than eight Fantasy points (six point per passing TD leagues) in the extra session. Harold Fannin Jr. did not have a target until OT!
YOU CAN DROP THEM: Juwan Johnson and Devaughn VeleJordyn Tyson played limited snaps in his NFL debut, and he was still second on the team in targets. Johnson caught a TD in OT but was otherwise slient. Vele needs big target volume to be good for Fantasy. Kansas City 35 – New York Jets 12WAS BETTER THAN THE NUMBERS: Patrick MahomesMahomes threw a TD to Travis Kelce, but it was ruled a backward pass and therefore a rushing TD for Kelce. He also completed a pass to Xavier Worthy at the 2-yard line and handed off to Kenneth Walker for a TD on the next play. This was nearly a huge game for Mahomes. BUYER BEWARE: Breece HallHall received 18 touches in his first game back from injury, but Braelon Allen played a lot more than Hall. Allen was the primary passing-downs back, dominated snaps late in the game (as the Jets were chasing points), and played all three snaps inside the 5-yard line. This kind of role makes Hall the definition of a trap back. 
FANTASY DUD: Adonai MitchellIf the connection between Mitchell and Geno Smith had been a little bit better, he could have caught two TDs today. Instead, Mitchell had zero catches on seven targets. We can shake this off and call it a bad game, but if Garrett Wilson returns next week, I don't think Fantasy managers will trust Mitchell. Los Angeles Rams 20 – Washington 13KEY INJURY: Puka Nacua hurt his knee late in the fourth quarter. Let's cross our fingers and hope it's nothing serious. GETTING WORRIED: Jayden DanielsWhy isn't he running? Daniels rushed for 103 yards against the Giants in Week 5. In the three games since, he has rushed for 49 yards. Unless he is injured, this is the kind of statistic I expect to show a positive regression. It's also fair to wonder how good he can be without Terry McLaurin. I wouldn't give up on him yet as his schedule looks pretty good in the near future, but I am certainly lowering expectations. 
Denver 26 – Carolina 21SURPRISING STUD: Bryce YoungI did not see this coming. The Panthers haven't been able to protect Young and were facing one of the best pass rushes in the NFL, yet Young scored 26.3 Fantasy points in six point per passing TD leagues and gives me confidence to start him next week against the Saints. He's not a must-start, but certainly is in the mix.NOT BUYING IT: Darren WallerTen targets, eight catches, 90 yards and a TD. I need to see him do it again before I consider adding him.  Detroit 19 – Miami 9GETTING CONCERNED: The Lions offense This one deserves some digging, and we'll do that during the week. The Lions have scored 19-20 points in 3 straight games against the Packers, Vikings and Dolphins. It's somewhat understandable in those first two matchups, but not against Miami.
LOSER: Ollie GordonI love the way he runs, and I love his workload. Gordon is always going to have a chance to score. But Gordon has seven catches this season. If the Dolphins are in bad game scripts, he is vulnerable to such performances. It's similar to what we've seen from Derrick Henry lately. Dallas 27 – Indianapolis 23LOSER: Ryan FlournoyTwo catches for 53 yards on three targets for Flournoy. We expected more targets and more production with George Pickens out. If Pickens misses another game, can you really trust Flournoy? I think he'll be better than this (especially if Jake Ferguson has to miss time), but he's certainly not a must-start. PLEASE TRADE HIM: Jonathan TaylorI mean the Colts, not Fantasy managers. Just get him off the Colts. Taylor has been a Fantasy dud two straight weeks, which coincides with the Quentin Nelson trade. Certainly, I don't think Nelson is the sole reason for it, and of course Taylor was denied a TD today because he lost his shoe and had to briefly leave the field. But this team is dreadful, and I don't like RBs on dreadful teams. If Taylor stays with the Colts, he's still a Top 12 RB. 
New York Giants 19 – Philadelphia 11NOTHING TO WORRY ABOUT: Malik NabersNabers nearly caught a TD and was shadowed by Eagles stud CB Quinyon Mitchell. He'll be fine going forward. LOSER: DeVonta SmithThe Eagles can't reliably complete forward passes. DeVonta Smith is currently averaging more than 17 PPR points per game, but I think he'll average fewer than 14 PPR points per game going forward (whenever he comes back). It's a shame. This could have been a great season for him.

title: Chiefs looking to trade for wide receiver, GM Brett Veach tells NFL on CBS' Tracy Wolfson - CBS Sports
description: Kansas City has one of the NFL's least-productive wide receiver corps in 2026
body:
Kansas City has one of the NFL's least-productive wide receiver corps in 2026
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Chiefs GM Brett Veach told NFL on CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson that Kansas City is looking to add a wide receiver ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, though "some of the major franchise players they've looked at are off the market," Wolfson reported during the Chiefs' Week 9 game against the Jets.
Wolfson specifically mentioned the lack of deep passing, something that's been a major issue ever since Tyquan Thornton suffered a significant injury in Week 4. Patrick Mahomes did not complete a single 20+ yard pass from Weeks 5-8 (three games), tying the longest streak of his career.Currently, the Chiefs are leaning on Xavier Worthy and Rashee Rice as their top wide receivers. Worthy entered Week 9 having recorded 25 or more receiving yards just twice this season, and Rice is more of a quick-game, yards-after-catch weapon. Other wide receivers on the roster are fifth-round rookie Cyrus Allen, 2025 fourth-round pick Jalen Royals, undrafted second-year player Andrew Armstrong and return specialist Nikko Remigio.Through eight weeks, only the Raiders' and Vikings' wide receivers had fewer receiving yards.There are several wide receivers thought to be available ahead of Tuesday's deadline, though, according to Wolfson's report, some of the biggest names floated might not be on the table. Veach and Co. will keep pushing before the clock strikes 4 pm. ET on Tuesday, marking the end of the trade period.
The Chiefs (5-2) had lost two straight entering Sunday.

title: Daniel Jones trade rumors: Colts tell QB he will not be dealt before NFL deadline, per report - CBS Sports
description: The 2-7 Colts have taken Daniel Jones off the market, even as Jonathan Taylor and several teammates remain names
body:
The 2-7 Colts have taken Daniel Jones off the market, even as Jonathan Taylor and several teammates remain names to watch
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Indianapolis Colts told quarterback Daniel Jones they will not trade him before Tuesday's deadline, according to Tom Pelissero.Indianapolis (2-7) received calls for Jones with the trade deadline looming. The Colts, who already traded offensive lineman Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers, remain among the central characters on the trade market. Most eyes will be on star running back Jonathan Taylor, who said a goodbye of sorts to Indianapolis after Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys, but Josh Downs and Grover Stewart are potential names to watch, too.Apparently, Jones will not be joining them. It's been a mess of a year in Indianapolis, which has already fired general manager Chris Ballard, and that has extended to Jones. This season, he has been among the league's worst quarterbacks.
Daniel Jones this seasonNFL rank (out of 30)Yards per attempt5.729thTD-Int6-1029thCompletion percentage60.3%26thYards per completion9.529thJones' surroundings have been far from ideal, with Alec Pierce -- signed to an extension this past offseason -- missing almost the entire season after aggravating the ankle injury he had surgery on this offseason. Currently, Keenan Allen leads the team in receptions (40), and Downs leads the team in receiving yards (354).The Vikings seemed to be a potential tie to Jones, who spent time with Minnesota's practice squad two seasons ago. Minnesota has struggled offensively with Kyler Murray and is starting Carson Wentz on Monday as Murray deals with a hamstring injury. It's unknown, though, which teams had been in contact regarding Jones' availability.
Jones, who is a team captain, signed a two-year, $88 million extension this past offseason, though the Colts have a potential out after this season that would leave them with $35.2 million of dead cap. Indianapolis does not own its first-round pick due to last season's Sauce Gardner trade, so perhaps the Colts envision keeping Jones around as a placeholder next year. Regardless, he will be around at least for the rest of this season.

body:
There are lots of ways to break down an NFL game, but sometimes, it's as simple as "my guy is better than your guy." The Jimmys and the Joes matter more than the X's and the O's.Or, rather, the Ja'Marrs and the Joes (and the Tees). The Bengals went to Spain and thumped the Falcons, 34-17, behind four total touchdowns (three passing, one rushing) by Joe Burrow. Ja'Marr Chase had 10 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins had five catches for 47 yards and two scores.Chase and Higgins are so, so good. CBS Sports NFL writer Jared Dubin had an excellent piece earlier this week about Higgins' breakout, but Sunday, Chase reminded everyone why he's either the best receiver or, at worst, one of the best wide receivers in the NFL. In the first half alone, Chase had eight catches for 142 yards and a score. He does it every which way: deep, intermediate, short. Over the middle or along the sideline. Open or contested catch. Yards after catch or before. Doesn't matter. This is receiving at its best.
Chase and Higgins are the best wide receiver duo in the NFL -- it's not close --and, halfway through the year, they have us leading our overreactions and reality checks with ...
Joe Burrow is the first-half MVP ...Overreaction or reality check: RealityHere's Burrow's start to the season:74% completion percentage (1st in NFL)23 passing touchdowns (1st in NFL)26 touchdowns accounted for (1st in NFL)According to CBS Sports research, Burrow is the first player ever with a 70% completion percentage and four total touchdowns in four straight games. Not coincidentally, the Bengals have won four straight.Burrow has great wide receivers, but that should not take away too much from his candidacy, especially when you consider how bad the running game is and how inconsistent the defense has been.There are a few things holding me back from declaring Burrow the MVP winner -- in terms of odds, he's currently right next to Josh Allen as the favorite (+210 at DraftKings, but that could move around depending on when you're reading this). There's a long way to go; the weather will turn, and Burrow's checkered health history is worth noting. But if we had to name an MVP right now, it'd be Burrow, who has been truly excellent.
... or you could give it to Jordan LoveOverreaction or reality check: RealityHere's Jordan Love's so far this season:2,618 passing yards (1st in NFL)40 completions of 20+ yards (1st in NFL)19 passing touchdowns (3rd in NFL)Thank goodness "first-half MVP" isn't a real award, because I have no clue how I'd vote. Love has supported an even more anemic rushing attack this season: Green Bay gets under 20% of its yards on the ground, on pace for the worst mark since the 1970 merger. And also, he's been hurt by the league's highest drop rate.Yes, Love has a better defense supporting him, but he has been stupendous, lifting Christian Watson and Matthew Golden into stardom alongside him. They became the first Green Bay wide receiver duo to both have 150+ yards and a touchdown in a single game as the Packers shredded the Patriots.Love has the NFL's most completions 20+ yards downfield (23), and his deep ball is truly a thing of beauty. 
Oh yeah, and Brock Purdy and Josh Allen have been pretty good, too. The MVP race will be a wild one.The Browns should stick with Shedeur Sanders as starterOverreaction or reality check: RealityMany times, the box score lies. Not so for Shedeur Sanders. You just have to make sure to read all of it:19-for-31 (fine)297 yards (good!)2 touchdowns, 0 interceptions (very good!)9.6 yards per attempt (also good!)5 sacks for 37 yards (bad!)10 carries for 28 yards (not great)The 23-22 loss to the Saints will leave a bad taste in the mouth after what was otherwise a solid performance, especially given the circumstances. Cleveland's offensive line was abysmal, as has been the case much of the year, and the run game didn't help at all. There were also multiple drops.
But there were several things Sanders delivered that Deshaun Watson simply doesn't. How about three completions on throws 30+ yards downfield? Watson has one ... all year!
Sanders also did excellently in several moments navigating the pressure. Was he great? No. The sacks are a major issue, and he invites some of the pressure on himself with how he holds onto the ball. But he also had an 11-yard scramble on a third-and-6 and, later, a 5-yard scramble on third-and-4.Furthermore, let's remember this was his first start of the year in a new system. After a very poor start, Sanders threw for 259 yards after halftime.
Coaches rarely bench players due to injury, so I wouldn't be surprised if Watson returns to the lineup. Todd Monken refused to talk about it postgame. But in this writer's eyes, Sanders should keep the job.The 'Dream Team' Rams are being held back by Matthew StaffordOverreaction or reality check: RealityThe Rams are above .500 for the first time this year after outlasting the Commanders, 20-13. The Rams force-fed Puka Nacua (19 targets for 14 catches, 150 yards and a touchdown) and got just enough for the run game. Myles Garrett came back in full force with three sacks and a forced fumble. At 5-4 and winners of three straight -- and with the Cardinals up next -- Los Angeles should feel OK.But Matthew Stafford just does not look good. Plain and simple. He threw an awful interception after locking in on Nacua, with no chance of completion.
He's throwing an awful interception seemingly every week. He has nine picks through nine games. This was last week's.
Stafford missed a ton of throws he made routinely during his 2025 MVP campaign. Sunday alone, he missed an open Tyler Higbee on an out-breaking route; he missed Tutu Atwell twice -- once wide, once high -- and missed Nacua once, too, this time low.Last year, Stafford completed 43% of his throws 20+ yards downfield and had a 10-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio on those throws. This year: 24% completion rate and a 1-to-3 touchdown-to-interception ratio.
The Rams can still be a good team. The defense looks excellent, and Garrett makes the pass rush truly terrifying. The Rams have found a physical run game during this winning streak, too. But at some point, they will need Stafford to play like his 2025 self, and it just doesn't look like he has that anymore.The Eagles should fire Nick SirianniOverreaction or reality check: OverreactionThe Eagles lost their seventh straight game Sunday, dropping an 19-11 eyesore to the Giants. It's Philadelphia's second-longest losing streak this century, and Nick Sirianni's bunch now sits at 2-7 on this dreadful year.The Eagles used their third different starting quarterback (Joe Milton) of the season, and he looked like ... well ... a third-string quarterback who didn't even start the year with the team, which is exactly what he is. He completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards and ran for 64 yards, balancing out some fun moments with several frustrating ones. The defense had a much better day overall, especially considering the poor efforts it had put forth the previous few weeks.
Listen, everything has gone wrong for the Eagles. Jalen Hurts is done for the year. The offensive line has been in upheaval ever since Week 1. DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley have been hurt. And that's precisely why the Eagles shouldn't fire Nick Sirianni, now or at any point this season. Philadelphia has a first-year offensive coordinator, Sean Mannion, who would be best served by a stable environment. Same with Milton, who should continue to start all year. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio does not want to be a head coach again at this point in his career.It's ok to have worst-case-scenario years and not make it worse, especially as you're just playing out the string. Maybe Sirianni gets fired after the year, but the team hasn't given up, and it needs what little stability it has.The NFC East race is overOverreaction or reality check: OverreactionThe Giants' win puts them at 5-2-1 on the season, a truly remarkable start. J.J. McCarthy wasn't good, but he didn't have any huge mistakes, and that's enough against a team like the Eagles.
The Cowboys avoided a DEFCON 1-level loss, surviving a mistake-riddled game to beat the Colts 27-23. Dallas lost a pair of fumbles in awful moments, had several terrible penalties and seemingly spent half the game trying to give it away. But it won and is now 4-5. Yes, that's 2.5 games back of New York, but it's not impossible.Should the Cowboys buy at the deadline? Probably not. But that hasn't stopped Jerry Jones before. More defensive help could be on the way. Could Dallas dangle George Pickens as a trade option to acquire some much-needed help on defense via a player-for-player trade? Joey Porter Jr. will get healthy, as will others. (That includes Pickens, if he stays.)I don't think the Cowboys are very good, but they might not need to be very good to win this division. A Week 17 showdown between the two teams still looms large, even if Dallas underwhelmed very much (again) in Week 9.It's over for the PanthersOverreaction or reality check: OverreactionMake it three straight losses for the Panthers, who are now 3-5 on the season. But if anything, this was by far the "best" of those three losses. Bryce Young had some very good moments, and Carolina actually out-gained Denver 353-312. The undermanned defense hung in there, and if it wasn't for an absolutely crazy endzone interception, this could have been a Carolina win.
Most importantly, the Panthers play in the NFC South, where no one is above .500. Carolina's still in it, even with another tally in the loss column.Nico Collins has a 'Catch of the Year' candidateOverreaction or reality check: RealitySpeaking of wild highlights:
The following trades should happenOverreaction or reality check: RealityThe trade deadline is Tuesday. Let's make some moves, both big and small:The Chiefs acquire George Pickens from the Cowboys. GM Brett Veach told NFL on CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson that Kansas City has been scouring the trade market for a wide receiver, though some big names have been made unavailable. Perhaps that extends to Pickens, but if not, Kansas City should be very aggressive trying to boost Patrick Mahomes' surroundings.While we're at it, the Chiefs acquire Andrew Wylie from the Commanders. Kansas City's offensive line is in seemingly constant rotation. Wylie isn't getting much action for Washington, but he has guard and tackle versatility and is a former Chief.... ORThe Patriots acquire Wylie from the Commanders. Or they acquire some other offensive lineman/linemen. New England's front five has been destroyed by injury.The Vikings acquire Jonathan Taylor from the Colts. Taylor all but said goodbye to Indianapolis. He should be saying hello to Minneapolis.The Jaguars acquire Grover Stewart from the Colts. I don't think the Jaguars should care if they need to pay the in-division tax. Stewart is a stout run defender, which is exactly what the Jaguars need after losing DaVon Hamilton for the season. Here are some other options.The Lions acquire Tariq Woolen. I've been beating this drum for a while. Woolen is on a one-year deal for an Eagles team going nowhere. Detroit is battling for a playoff spot and needs secondary reinforcements.

schema.headline: NFL Week 9 overreactions: Joe Burrow or Jordan Love for MVP? Shedeur Sanders deserves to remain starter? - CBS Sports

title: Jonathan Taylor says goodbye to Indianapolis as trade deadline nears: 'Just know it was a pleasure' - CBS Sports
description: Taylor expressed gratitude to the city and fans following Sunday's loss as Indianapolis faces a Tuesday deadline
body:
Taylor expressed gratitude to the city and fans following Sunday's loss as Indianapolis faces a Tuesday deadline decision
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL's trade deadline is Tuesday, and speculation around some of the biggest names in the sport has reached a fever pitch. No player has been talked about more over the past few weeks than Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, who may or may not have just played his last game for the organization that selected him No. 41 overall in the 2020 NFL Draft.Taylor's Colts fell to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, 27-23, and the running back rushed 13 times for 46 yards while adding 18 yards receiving on five receptions. In the locker room, Taylor was asked about his thoughts on whether this was indeed his final game with the Colts or not. "I think you play every game like it's your last, but at the end of the day this has been a spot where I grew up," Taylor said. "I think I mentioned this to you guys — like you go to college, you're a young man, but you really grew up, you started a family and you really embraced this city, the people, and you're just like ... this place helped shape me into the man I am today. If it is [my last game], I'm very grateful for the city of Indianapolis."Taylor was then asked what he hopes fans remember most about him if he were to be traded in the next 48 hours. "I just hope that they appreciate and know that I appreciate them and it was a pleasure to put on display not only my hard work but the team's hard work each and every single week, each and every single year," Taylor said. "Just know it was a pleasure." 
For a franchise that featured Hall of Famers like Edgerrin James, Marshall Faulk and Eric Dickerson, Taylor is one of the best running backs to ever call himself a Colt. He's the organization's leader in rushing touchdowns with 77 and ranks No. 2 in rushing yards with 8,254. Taylor's 89.2 rushing yards per game entering this week ranked fifth in NFL history.When the Colts traded offensive guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers, speculation increased that they could deal their star running back. According to Jay Glazer of Fox Sports, the New York Giants offered a second- and fifth-round pick for Taylor a couple of weeks ago. That offer is now reportedly off the table unless there's a lower price. There are other teams that could use a good running back. The Green Bay Packers registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. Josh Jacobs injured his hand vs. the New England Patriots, and he hasn't exactly looked electric in his return from the commissioner's exempt list. The 6-1 Minnesota Vikings could potentially turn from pretender to contender if they added a weapon like Taylor, and the same could be said for the Denver Broncos.
Ultimately, maybe the Colts value Taylor more than any other team. It's possible he's not moved at the trade deadline. But he said his goodbyes in the locker room on Sunday just in case.

schema.headline: Jonathan Taylor says goodbye to Indianapolis as trade deadline nears: 'Just know it was a pleasure' - CBS Sports

title: NFL Week 9 winners and losers: Ja'Marr Chase, Packers WRs go ballistic while Drake Maye's turnover woes return - CBS Sports
description: Ja'Marr Chase has been in the top tier of NFL wide receivers since he entered the league with the Bengals in 2021 and proved on Sunday w
body:
Ja'Marr Chase has been in the top tier of NFL wide receivers since he entered the league with the Bengals in 2021 and proved on Sunday why he belongs in the superstar echelon. Week 9 brought the absolute best version of the three-time All-Pro. He showed off his pass-catching prowess to an international audience with the best first half of his career in the 2026 Madrid Game.Back on American soil were a number of other star-caliber performances but also a handful of lowlights. The Washington Commanders were among those teams who left something to be desired when they fell to 2-5-1 on the year, and on an individual level, Drake Maye turned in a dreadful performance and tossed three interceptions for the second time this season.For every standout showing, there is typically an inverse effort that is equally as poor. Here are the biggest winners and losers from Sunday's Week 9 action across the NFL.Winner: Ja'Marr Chase's historic first halfThe final box score shows that Chase had himself a massive day in Madrid. The Bengals receiver caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in the 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons and was integral in his franchise securing its first win on international soil. Far more impressive than his totals, however, was the percentage of that production that came in the first half alone.
Chase hauled in eight of his receptions in the game's first half hour. The touchdown and 142 of his yards also came in the opening half. The yardage was the most in any first half of Chase's tremendous career and the most in a first half by a Bengals wide receiver since 1988.In the process, Chase joined Randy Moss as the only two wide receivers in NFL history with at least seven touchdowns in each of their first six seasons.Most career games with 10+ receptions, 100+ receiving yards, 1+ receiving TDDavante Adams: 16Ja'Marr Chase: 13Keenan Allen: 12Antonio Brown: 12Loser: Drake MayeThere is a three-man tie for the most turnovers in football, and Drake Maye joined that group on the heels of a disastrous showing in the Patriots' defeat. His 13 turnovers match those of Daniel Jones and Justin Herbert, who own the two lowest passer ratings in the NFL. His season-long tally ballooned with three interceptions against the Packers, and it hardly took any time for him to put one in the ledger, as the first pick came in the game's opening minute.
Maye settled in following a brutal start to the year and had only tossed one interception in his last four games heading into Week 9. But he reverted back to the tendencies that made him a major disappointment in September, and the Patriots suffered because of it.Winners: Matthew Golden and Christian WatsonThe Green Bay Packers might just have two star wide receivers. It helps to have a red-hot quarterback in Jordan Love throwing to them, but Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have both taken sizable steps forward this season and reached a new and historic level as a tandem in the 45-27 rout of the New England Patriots. They combined for 17 catches, 335 receiving yards and two touchdowns and became the first pair of Packers teammates with 150 yards and a touchdown apiece in the same game since 1942. They are also the fourth duo in the NFL since 2020 with 160 yards and a touchdown each.Most of Golden's work came in the first quarter. He was remarkable in the opening quarter with six grabs for 126 yards and his touchdown.
This receiving group is among the reasons why the Packers are in play for the hotly contested NFC North title, and the passing game looks capable of going toe-to-toe with any in the league. That could pay dividends in the postseason.Loser: Commanders' end-of-game decisionsThe same team that botched a last-second situation earlier in the year and thus settled for a tie instead of a potential win delivered another head-scratcher a few weeks later. The Commanders needed a touchdown to force overtime or take the lead against the Rams and had mere seconds to obtain it when they made two questionable calls.With eight seconds to play in a 20-13 game, quarterback Jayden Daniels took a deep shot and left the ball short of the goal line. That would have been a reasonable throw if the Commanders had any timeouts at their disposal, but they were out of them at that point of the fourth quarter. A completion in that spot would have ended the game. Then, on the final play of the afternoon, Washington dialed up a hook-and-ladder play instead of a Hail Mary, which came up well shy of the end zone. Rather than having Daniels chuck the ball 31 yards, they looked for something underneath that was not there.
Coach Dan Quinn and offensive coordinator David Blough have drawn significant scrutiny, and those end-of-game decisions will not pull them out from under the microscope.Winner: Rams' defensive frontIt took until Week 9, but the Los Angeles Rams were finally able to unleash a ridiculously talented defensive line duo of Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald. Garrett made his first appearance since Week 1 as he returned from injured reserve and completed his comeback from an in-season knee surgery. It was his first game with Donald, who joined the lineup in Week 2.Garrett said in advance of the 20-13 win over the Commanders that opposing offensive lines would have to pick their poison when dealing with the one-two punch of future Hall of Famers and that they would have fun exploiting any one-on-one matchups that came their way. He did just that when he racked up three sacks and a forced fumble in his first game back. It was his eighth career three-sack performance.
Loser: Kirk Cousins' trade valueIf Sunday was the last time Kirk Cousins suited up in a Las Vegas Raiders uniform, it would be a sour ending to his brief tenure with the franchise. Although the team reportedly wants to keep him, Cousins' name has been thrown around in trade discussions ahead of Tuesday's deadline. Perhaps the combination of the Raiders' unwillingness to move him and his turnover issues in a 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers will keep him in town, though.Cousins threw three interceptions and is now tied for the most three-pick games in the NFL since 2020. Only Tua Tagovailoa has as many such outings.It would be a steep drop for Cousins to go from a potential trade piece and starter for a contending team to a second-string quarterback, but if the offense flounders in the weeks to come and the Raiders slip out of the postseason hunt, coach Klint Kubiak could hand the keys to the offense to Fernando Mendoza. The No. 1 overall pick will likely get a look as the starter before the season is done. Any further struggles from Cousins may expedite that.
Winner: Shedeur SandersShedeur Sanders' terrific individual effort came with the caveat that it did not result in a win. The Cleveland Browns quarterback showed the makings of a viable starter in the 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints, though. That is a development that gives the Browns some flexibility moving forward if Deshaun Watson falters upon his return from the concussion protocol. And it could even lead to an internal quarterback controversy if any of the Browns decision-makers view Sanders' 297-yard, two-touchdown performance as a successful audition for the job.Even in defeat, Sanders came through in the clutch for the Browns. According to Next Gen Stats, the second-year quarterback was 4-for-12 for 141 yards and two touchdowns when under pressure in the second half and overtime. In his final three drives, Sanders connected with rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion for a 64-yard go-ahead touchdown pass with 5:21 to play, moved the ball into field goal range to send the game to overtime and threw a touchdown pass to Harold Fannin Jr. at the end of overtime. That 39-yarder to the tight end would have been a game-winner if the Browns pulled off the 2-point conversion.Winners: Offenses that survived quarterback injury scaresA pair of division title contenders watched their lives flash before their eyes. Two quarterback injuries ended up being much less severe than they appeared in the moment, and that gave the Chiefs and New York Giants a sigh of relief, because they looked bad. Patrick Mahomes did not miss a single snap despite sustaining an arm injury, while J.J. McCarthy returned to his game after less than a quarter's worth of evaluation on the sideline and in the locker room with a hip issue.
Mahomes took a heavy hit to his throwing arm from Jets standout rookie David Bailey and coughed up the ball for a strip sack. He gripped his  throwing arm as he ran to the sideline in immense discomfort, but he was back out with the offense on their next drive and led the unit to a 21-0 second half shutout in a 23-point win.McCarthy missed nearly the entire third quarter of the Giants' 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, and it was Jameis Winston who led a go-ahead touchdown drive in his absence. But he bounced back from a hard hit to his hip and kept the lead intact during the final period. In just his second start with the team since his arrival via trade, he guided the Giants to their first win in Philadelphia in 13 years and kept them in first place in the NFC East.Loser: Chargers' touchdown-less streakIt was another disaster of a week for the Los Angeles Chargers, but at least they scored a touchdown. In fact, they scored two. The most woeful offense in the NFL had gone 12 quarters (tied for the longest drought in franchise history) and 37 possessions (the most since the 2023-24 Chargers) without a trip to the end zone until Justin Herbert connected with Quentin Johnston on an explosive 58-yarder.
That strike was far too little and far too late to avert another loss, though. The Chargers are still the only winless team in the league and are now 0-8 following their 44-22 defeat at the hands of the Houston Texans.Winner: C.J. StroudFor the second time in his career, C.J. Stroud racked up at least 350 yards and five touchdowns in a game. He is the only player in Texans history to have done so twice. The breakout quarterback finished the day with 384 yards in the drubbing of the Chargers, which keeps him firmly on pace to outperform the career-best production he posted in his Pro Bowl-caliber rookie season in 2023.Stroud was the NFL's passing yards per game leader in his debut season, and he also paced the league in interception rate. Following two underwhelming campaigns, he is back in that same form and could contend for the No. 1 spot on the leaderboard in both categories again. Houston's 3-5 record overshadows some of his individual success, but if he keeps playing like this, the Texans will have a chance to pull themselves out of a deep hole and compete for a spot in the playoffs.
Winner: Close-game BroncosIt takes some luck to win one-score games in the NFL, but good teams create their own luck. The Denver Broncos are a good team. Their 26-21 win over the Carolina Panthers extended their winning streak in one-possession regular-season games to 16, which is the longest such streak in NFL history. The last time they fell short in one of those tight situations was all the way back in Week 3 of the 2025 season.This one nearly got away from them, actually. The Broncos built a 26-14 lead with 5:41 to play but surrendered a touchdown and watched as the Panthers advanced to the 36-yard line in the final two minutes. A strip sack ended Carolina's rally and made edge rusher Nik Bonnitto the latest standout to play the hero role in this stretch of clutch wins.All but one of Denver's seven wins this year have come by seven points or fewer. Doubters will argue that this is an unsustainable way to win, but Sean Payton's team just keeps pulling it off.Broncos' 2026 one-score winsWeek 2: W 20-13 vs. JaguarsWeek 3: W 30-26 vs. RamsWeek 5: W 23-17 at ChargersWeek 6: W 17-14 (OT) at SeahawksWeek 8: W 28-24 vs. ChiefsWeek 9: W 26-21 at PanthersLoser: Harrison ButkerThe silver lining for the Kansas City Chiefs is that their kicking woes did not haunt them in their three-score win over the New York Jets. But with the way things have gone on special teams this season -- and even dating back to last year -- one has to wonder how long Harrison Butker will keep his job. His persistent struggles are bound to cost the Chiefs in close games during the second half of the season and into the playoffs unless he turns a corner or the team removes him in favor of a more consistent field goal kicker.Butker missed a field goal attempt at the end of the first half, but an offsides penalty negated the failed kick. He then missed the second try from five yards closer.Only eight games into the season, Butker has already missed more attempts this year (seven) than in any single season during his career. He has now also missed 17 field goal tries since the start of the 2025 campaign. His miscues led the Chiefs to add Justin Tucker to their practice squad last month. It may be a matter of time before the team elevates Tucker to the active roster and ends the Butker era.Winners: PuntersNo team ever wants its punter on the field, but three squads made the most of fourth-down situations on Sunday. The Miami Dolphins and Detroit Lions turned their punters into offensive threats with a fake punt apiece, and in doing so, their matchup became the first game in NFL history wherein both teams' punters completed a pass.Jack Fox of the Lions was the first of the two to successfully pick up a first down through the air. From his own 29-yard line, he threw a strike to Tay Martin for 11 yards and a new set of downs. Fox is now 5-of-6 passing for his career with 72 yards, and each of his completions resulted in a first down. The Dolphins pulled off a trick of their own in the fourth quarter when Bradley Pinon floated a ball to a wide-open Kaytron Allen, who rattled off a 46-yard gain on fourth-and-3 from Miami's own 36.
Even regularly designed punts turned into highlights this week. Although Braden Mann was also responsible for a -2-yard punt, he flipped field position in the Eagles' favor with an 86-yard punt, which was the longest in the NFL since 2001 and the 10th-longest in franchise history.

schema.headline: NFL Week 9 winners and losers: Ja'Marr Chase, Packers WRs go ballistic while Drake Maye's turnover woes return - CBS Sports

title: Michigan fires Jason Beck: Wolverines will owe significant buyout after parting with struggling OC in Year 1 - CBS Sports
description: A dismal 15-6 loss to rival Michigan State proved to be the breaking point for a unit ranking near the bottom of
body:
A dismal 15-6 loss to rival Michigan State proved to be the breaking point for a unit ranking near the bottom of the FBS in scoring and total offense
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Michigan fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, the school announced on Sunday, one day after a 15-6 loss to Michigan State in which the Wolverines managed only 192 total offensive yards. Offensive line coach Jim Harding will serve as interim offensive coordinator for the remainder of the season.Beck, the nation's highest-paid offensive coordinator, came with head coach Kyle Whittingham after a successful year together at Utah last season. That success never translated in Ann Arbor, however, on a 5-4 Michigan team that is one of the most disappointing in the country. The loss to Michigan State was the final straw. "The results have not matched our desired outcome, and I felt that a change in leadership was required for our offense," Whittingham said Sunday. "We need to put our offensive players and the entire team in the best possible position to be successful."We appreciate the hard work and effort that Jason has dedicated to the program. Jason is a great man and coach, and unfortunately, it did not work out the way that we wanted it to at Michigan. We wish Jason and his family nothing but the best in the future."Michigan already made a quarterback change earlier in the season, benching highly paid former five-star quarterback Bryce Underwood in favor of freshman Tommy Carr. The offense never really got going, however, and ranked 125th in passing offense, 126th in scoring offense and 132nd in total offense out of 138 FBS teams.
Beck's firing comes with a significant financial hit for Michigan. The Wolverines will owe Beck as much as $10.2 million to buy out a three-year deal that paid him $2.8 million this season and was set to go up to more than $3 million the next two seasons, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. It could be the most expensive assistant coach buyout ever, though it is subject to offset mitigation. The pressure had been building on Whittingham to make a move as the offense continued to flounder this season. The noise got particularly loud after a 13-6 loss to Indiana in which the Wolverines managed only 57 rushing yards on 42 carries. Michigan had one of the nation's most expensive rosters, sources told CBS Sports, and had especially invested big on the offensive side of the ball. Beck was never able to fit the pieces he acquired into the system he wanted to run, however. It will be interesting to see whether it provides a spark to an offense that is in desperate need of one. As CBS Sports first reported last month, Whittingham's job security could also be in question. Michigan is in the middle of an AD search to replace outgoing AD Warde Manuel and would like to find its next athletic department leader before deciding on Whittingham, according to sources. But it is not out of the realm of possibilities that Whittingham could be one-and-done in Ann Arbor, especially if he continues to lose games.
"I think they know this isn't the long term," one industry source told CBS Sports. "It's just, do you rip it up after one year?"

schema.headline: Michigan fires Jason Beck: Wolverines will owe significant buyout after parting with struggling OC in Year 1 - CBS Sports

title: Jon Rahm beats Rory McIlroy to win Abu Dhabi Championship in first start since LIV Golf exit - CBS Sports
description: A back-nine surge carried the Spaniard to a two-shot victory over Tyrrell Hatton at Yas Links
body:
A back-nine surge carried the Spaniard to a two-shot victory over Tyrrell Hatton at Yas Links
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When one door closes, another one opens. For Jon Rahm, it led him into the winner's circle for his first meaningful victory since his 2023 Masters triumph. In his debut start at the Abu Dhabi Championship at Yas Links GC, the Spaniard could do no wrong as he reached 23 under par for the tournament, winning by two strokes over his former LIV Golf mate, Tyrrell Hatton. Rahm's victory marks his 11th DP World Tour title in just 92 starts, making him the third fastest to that number behind only Tiger Woods and Seve Ballesteros. He also now has six Rolex Series events to his name -- breaking a tie with Hatton for the most -- this one carrying significant weight one week ahead of the DP World Tour Championship. "It means a lot," Rahm said. "Still almost not letting myself believe it. It's been quite a while since I've played good in a DP World Tour event. And in my last showing, if you don't count the withdrawals, I think I finished last. So, from last to first is a pretty good feeling.  "As far as I'm concerned, except the shot on 17, I played a pretty flawless back nine. It was really, really solid. Never in danger of making a bogey except for one hole. ... That 6-iron [on 15] is a contender for shot of the year for me. After everything that's gone on and some poor play and some battles, mentally, with a lot of the noise, to come back out after a little bit of rest and having a new addition to the family, it's quite special. I only wish they were here to celebrate with me." 
Although Rahm called LIV Golf home in 2026, the former world No. 1 still has an opportunity to call himself the Race to Dubai champion on the DP World Tour. Should he run the table in the postseason and win the DP World Tour Championship next week, Rahm would need Rory McIlroy to finish worse than second place and current Race to Dubai leader, Eugenio Chacarra, to finish outside eighth place, according to the DP World Tour broadcast. Rahm has won the DP World Tour Championship on three previous occasions; he also captured the Race to Dubai in 2019. "I didn't think I would ever have a chance to win it," Rahm said. "Very excited. Actually gives me a little extra incentive next week. I really didn't think I was going to have a chance. Those are better odds than I expected, so [I'm] looking forward to it, and hopefully I can get my fourth one." 
Rahm was among four players tied for the lead heading into the back nine as his playing partners, Hatton and Francesco LaPorta, applied pressure while McIlroy made his move a group ahead. McIlroy ultimately fell off the pace with a bogey on No. 15, while LaPorta played Nos. 12-13 in 4-over fashion to drop out of contention. That left Rahm and Hatton to duke it out over the finishing stretch. Rahm just about sealed the deal with his approach shot into the par-4 15th. Not all is lost for McIlroy as he seeks to capture a record eighth Race to Dubai crown next week. The six-time major champion just about halved his deficit to Chacarra with his third-place finish at 19 under and leapfrogged Patrick Reed in the standings to position himself No. 2 in the season-long race with four rounds to go. 
Reed sits in third place in the Race to Dubai after leading the competition for most of the season with Casey Jarvis and Aaron Rai rounding out the top five. Rahm made a massive move from No. 51 to No. 6 thanks to his win and eyes even more next week when attention shifts to Dubai. "It's a pretty familiar spot for me going into the DP World Tour Championship, and I'm excited for it," McIlroy said. "That was the goal coming into these two weeks to try to catch Eugenio and Patrick and try to win The Race to Dubai again. Yeah, it would have been great to win this week and give myself not as much of a deficit or even a lead but still feel like I'm right in there with a great chance."

title: Blades Brown emerges as youngest PGA Tour winner in nearly a century - CBS Sports

body:
Brown, 19, erased a seven-shot deficit with a closing 63 before outlasting Ben James in a two-hole playoff at the World Wide Technology Championship
        
        
                                                                                                            
                                                    By
                                                
                                                            STATS
                                                    
                    
                                    
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:57 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    
            
    
        LOS CABOS, Mexico (AP) -- Blades Brown became the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years Sunday when the 19-year-old rallied from a seven-shot deficit with a 9-under 63 and beat Ben James with a birdie on the second playoff hole in the World Wide Technology Championship.Brown became the youngest winner since Charles Kocsis won the Michigan Open in 1931 when he was 18, a tournament that was considered a regional event in the early years of the PGA.James lost a four-shot lead going into the final round at El Cardonal at Diamante and then showed his moxie by smoking a 285-yard shot into 20 feet on the par-5 18th and making eagle to salvage a 70 and force the playoff.But he missed an 8-foot putt on the second playoff hole, and Brown made his 3-footer.
"I'm so obsessed with this game. It tests you in so many ways," said Brown, who graduated high school in January. "I love golf, all the stuff that goes into it and I can't wait for what's next."For a sleepy FedEx Cup Fall event on the southern tip of Baja California, this was pure theater between two players from the next generation. James was the No. 1 player in the PGA Tour University ranking last season. Brown make a surprising choice to turn pro two years ago while a junior in high school.Brown was tested even more by going through two bags of golf balls on the range waiting to see if the two-shot lead he had over James would hold, and then going back out to the 18th to decide it.
On the first extra hole, their approach shots were side-by-side, separated by about 3 feet, and both narrowly missed eagle chances. They returned to the 18th tee and their drives were next to each other. Both came up just short of the green.James nearly holed his pitch and saw it run out 8 feet. Brown, who had a similar pitch in regulation that he hit to 6 feet for a closing birdie, this time came up 3 feet short. James' birdie putt grazed the right edge, and Brown poured in the winner.They have known each since their junior days and Brown figures this is the start.
"I got him this time, but I'm sure we'll be battling it out for years to come," he said.With eight players separated by two shots on the back nine, Brown ran off three straight birdies to share the lead and then left the mistakes to everyone else. He hit a superb pitch for birdie on the final hole to post at 23-under 265.That put him one shot ahead of Michael Kim, who played with the Tennessee teen and made birdie from 12 feet for 64 right before Brown made his putt.
Brown earned his PGA Tour card for 2027 by finishing among the top 20 on the Korn Ferry Tour points list. Now he has a two-year exemption, which puts him in the elite Championship Series when the PGA Tour's new model begins in 2028.The victory also assures Brown of his first major next year at the PGA Championship.It was another setback for James, who in 13 starts since turning pro has five finishes in the top five, and two runner-up finishes.
Denny McCarthy, winless in nine years in 240 starts on the PGA Tour, made a 30-foot birdie putt on the 13th hole to take the lead. But he hit a pedestrian pitch to the par-5 14th and had to settle for par. With a wedge in hand from the 15th fairway, he came up some 40 feet short and three-putted for a bogey.McCarthy's tee shot on the 17th was right of the 18th tee box, he put his next shot off a dirt path into a hazard and made double bogey. He shot 69.
